en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.intro01: In Dune: Imperium, you take the role of a House Leader vying against rival Houses for control of the planet Arrakis, sole source of the most valuable resource in the Known Universe - the spice melange.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.intro02: In this tutorial, you are Paul of House Atreides. Your father, Duke Leto Atreides, will prepare you for the challenges that await your House on Arrakis.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.vp01: You have much to learn, Paul. Your first lesson: Power is measured in Victory Points. The House with the most will rule.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.cards01: Wise use of Imperium cards will be a vital skill. You and your rivals each begin the game with a shuffled starting deck and draw five cards at the beginning of every round.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent01: Imperium cards have two purposes. The first is sending Agents out in our service. That's called taking an Agent turn, and you'll take multiple each round.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent02: With two Agents here, it seems I'll be able to take two Agent turns this round. Where can I send them?
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent03: Let's begin with the Spice Trade and City board spaces of Arrakis.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent04.pc: To send an Agent to a board space, first choose a card to play. Hold your cursor over your Reconnaissance card.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent04.mobile: To send an Agent to a board space, first choose a card to play. Tap and hold your Reconnaissance card.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent05: Notice that Imperium cards have two boxes. During an Agent turn, you only use the top section, called the Agent box, including its Agent icons. Reconnaissance has a City Agent icon but no other Agent abilities.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent06: Once you've chosen a card, you can play it to a board space with a matching Agent icon.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent08: Now I release over Arrakeen to send my Agent!
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent09: Well done - your Agent is in place in Arrakeen. The icons on the space indicate what it does.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent10: One effect of Arrakeen is to allow you to recruit a troop. This Combat unit will join your garrison, which begins the game with three troops in it.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent11: You also get to draw a card from your deck into your hand.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent12.pc: Your first Agent turn is over. To send another Agent, you'll need to wait until your next turn. Select the End Turn button.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent12.mobile: Your first Agent turn is over. To send another Agent, you'll need to wait until your next turn. Tap the End Turn button.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-2.newturn: Normally, your opponents would take their turns after yours. For now, however, we'll move on to your second turn of the round.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-2.spice01: Show me you've been paying attention. How would you harvest spice from Hagga Basin?
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-2.spice02: My Dune, the Desert Planet cards have a icon - I'll drag one to Hagga Basin to send my second Agent there.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-2.spice03: Good. However, did you notice the water icon beneath the space's Agent icon? Certain board spaces require you to first pay resources to send an Agent there.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-2.spice04: I see. In sending an Agent to Hagga Basin, I spend a water and gain spice.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal01: That's right. With no more Agents available, you're done taking Agent turns this round. You must now take a different type of turn - a Reveal turn.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal02: During a Reveal turn, you only use the bottom section of your Imperium cards, called the Reveal box, which contains a card's Reveal effects.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal03.pc: Unlike an Agent turn, at the start of a Reveal turn you play all the remaining cards in your hand. Select Reveal to take your Reveal turn.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal03.mobile: Unlike an Agent turn, at the start of a Reveal turn you play all the remaining cards in your hand. Tap Reveal to take your Reveal turn.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal04: This is the Imperium Row. During your Reveal turn, you may spend Persuasion gained from Reveal effects on the cards you revealed to acquire cards from here, improving your deck.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal04b: But cards I used on previous turns this round to send Agents don't contribute their Reveal effects.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal04c: Indeed. As you see, you've gained Persuasion from the cards you've revealed.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal05: ...Which I can spend to acquire cards that I'll draw and use in future rounds.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal06: Precisely. A card's Persuasion cost appears in its upper right corner.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal06b: Drag our Warmaster, Gurney Halleck's card to the blue acquire area to acquire it for .
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.deck01: Cards you acquire go to your discard pile. At the end of your Reveal turn, so do all the cards you played that round.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.deck02: One last thing: When your deck is empty and you need to draw cards, your discard pile is shuffled to form your new deck - including any cards you've acquired.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.deck03: A summary of the Imperium Row is available for reference.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.endround01: Duke Leto! I see you are preparing young Paul for leadership. Is it time to begin his training in the art of combat?
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.endround02: He's ready. Paul, end your turn and I will relinquish you to Gurney's capable hands.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.intro01: Attention, Paul Atreides! Look at the spice fields of Arrakis and tell me what you see.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.maker01: A test? I see... more spice has appeared in some of the deserts - but not in Hagga Basin, where I sent an Agent.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.maker02: Correct. Spice blooms erupt regularly on Arrakis. At the end of every round, each of the three Maker spaces gains 1 bonus spice if they weren't harvested.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.rival01: Now begins your true test: House Harkonnen. We have many rivals, and the Harkonnen are the most ruthless.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.rival02: Count Glossu Rabban! They call him "Beast." He's my opponent?
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.turnorder01: Just a simulacrum. He takes his turn before you, as indicated by the First Player marker. It rotates between Leaders each round.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.turnorder02: You pitiful Atreides are unworthy of Arrakis! Its spice belongs to House Harkonnen, and I will claim it!
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.blocking01: Only one Agent can be on a space at a time, meaning that in addition to claiming the bonus spice at Imperial Basin, Beast has blocked you from sending an Agent there this round.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.conflict01: Now it's your turn and time for you to learn about Conflicts. There's a new one each round and every House may contest it.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.conflict02.pc: The Conflict card shows what's at stake. Hold your cursor over it for a closer look.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.conflict02.mobile: The Conflict card shows what's at stake. Tap and hold it for a closer look.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.conflict03: Conflicts reward the Leaders with the highest strength in the Conflict at the end of the round. Conflicts are a crucial source of Victory Points and other resources.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.conflict03b: This Conflict awards a <sprite name="VictoryPoint"> Victory Point to the winner, <sprite name="Water"> water to 2nd place, and <sprite name="Spice_1"> spice to 3rd.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.conflict04: You use troops to fight Conflicts. You have some in your garrison now, but their strength won't count until they're deployed to the Conflict.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.signet01: Use your Signet Ring to send an Agent to Carthag. This will give you an opportunity to deploy some of your garrisoned troops.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.signet02: When you send an Agent, you also get the effects in your card's Agent box. Each Leader's Signet Ring has a unique Agent effect: yours draws a card.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.intrigue01.pc: Carthag gave you a new kind of card: an Intrigue card. Hold your cursor over it to take a look.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.intrigue01.mobile: Carthag gave you a new kind of card: an Intrigue card. Tap and hold it to take a look.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.intrigue02: Intrigue cards are used once, then discarded. They come in three types: this one is a Plot card, meaning you can use it at any time during one of your turns. Hold onto it for later.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.deploy01: Now we can prepare for the Conflict, young Atreides. Certain board spaces, like Carthag, are Combat spaces.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.deploy02: Not just Carthag - it looks like every board space on Arrakis is a Combat space.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.deploy03: They are. That means they'll all allow you to deploy troops from your garrison to the Conflict.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.deploy03b: Deploying doesn't happen automatically. When you're ready, select Deploy Units.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.deploy03b.mobile: Deploying doesn't happen automatically. When you're ready, press Deploy Units.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.deploy04: A Combat space lets you deploy any troops you've recruited that turn, plus up to two more troops from your garrison.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.deploy05.pc: You just recruited a troop from Carthag, so this turn you can deploy up to three troops. Select the deploy area three times, then Confirm.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.deploy05.mobile: You just recruited a troop from Carthag, so this turn you can deploy up to three troops. Tap the deploy area three times, then Confirm.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.strength01: Each troop you have in the Conflict adds <sprite name="Strength"><sprite name="Strength"> to your strength, which will determine who wins the Conflict's rewards.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.strength02: Now, end your turn and let's see how Beast responds.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.strength03: You dare challenge me on the battlefield? I will crush you!
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-2.gurney01: Beast deployed more troops to the Conflict! His forces once again outnumber mine.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-2.gurney02.pc: Yes, but I've got something he won't see coming. Hold your cursor over my card.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-2.gurney02.mobile: Yes, but I've got something he won't see coming. Tap and hold my card.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-2.gurney03: My card's Reveal effects include the ability to spend Solari to recruit two more troops - and lets you deploy them to the Conflict immediately.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-2.soilari01: Solari is the currency of the Imperium and you'll need to look for opportunities beyond Arrakis to earn some. One option is to make a deal with CHOAM, the Imperium's monopolistic mercantile organization.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-2.solari02: One of the two CHOAM board spaces allows you to exchange <sprite name="Spice"> spice for <sprite name="Solari"> Solari; keep it in mind for the future.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-2.solari02b: For now, consider the other CHOAM space. Use Dune, the Desert Planet to send an Agent to Secure Contract.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-2.solari03: Done! I've secured the necessary funds from CHOAM.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.moretroops01: Your days near an end, Paul Atreides. My blade is eager to meet your throat.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.moretroops02: Ignore the Harkonnen's bluster and reveal your hand.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.moretroops03: You revealed two Daggers. Each of their Reveal effects gives you a sword that adds 1 to your strength if you have at least one troop deployed to the Conflict.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.moretroops04: It's time to spring the trap. Select my card's Reveal effect to use it.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.moretroops04.mobile: It's time to spring the trap. Tap my card's Reveal effect to use it.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.moretroops05: Deploy both of your new troops and Confirm.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.moretroops06: Your so-called warriors multiply like so many vermin!
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.thufir01: Beast is raging and the Conflict is imminent. Before it starts, finish taking your Reveal turn.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.thufir02: Paul Atreides! I am here, ready to continue your lessons once you acquire my card.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.thufir03: My trusted tutor, Thufir Hawat. I would, but I don't have enough Persuasion.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.thufir04: Don't you? You've forgotten your Intrigue card. Drag it to the board to play it now.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.thufir05: The Mentat is clever. Now you can acquire his card and, thanks to your Intrigue card, you get to place it on top of your deck to draw next. Do so now.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.thufir06: Prepare yourself - it's time for battle. End your turn and show this Harkonnen brute the might of House Atreides!
en_US.tutorial1.turn2.conflict01: I'm DEFEATED?! This miserable skirmish is yours - but it will be your last taste of victory.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2.conflict02: Well done, Paul. By winning that Conflict, you earned your first Victory Point.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2.conflict03: Win or lose, all troops deployed to the Conflict are lost. Be careful not to overcommit, because future rounds will bring further Conflicts.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2.conflict04: You've performed admirably. Rest briefly, then we'll pick up right where we left off.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-1.factions01: You and Gurney Halleck have shrewdly faced the Harkonnen threat. Now it's my duty to prepare you for the broader and subtler battlefield: Imperial politics.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-1.factions02: There are four great Factions in the Imperium. When you send an Agent to a Faction board space, you not only gain the effects shown, you also gain an Influence with that Faction.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-1.fremen01: For example, the Fremen are experts in desert survival and able to find water where no one else would.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-1.fremen02: To send an Agent to a Faction space, you must play a card with that Faction's Agent icon. Diplomacy has all four Faction icons - drag it to Stillsuits.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-1.fremen03: By using this Fremen space, you not only gained , but also 1 Influence with the Fremen. This is shown on their Influence track.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-1.fremen04: Both Fremen board spaces are also Combat spaces, so take this opportunity to deploy the two troops in your garrison to the Conflict.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-1.fremen05: Well done. Your father, the Duke, believes the Fremen could be powerful allies - but so could any Faction. On your next turn we will engage another.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-2.bg01: The witches of the <sprite name="BeneGesserit"> Bene Gesserit are secretive but powerful. Having their support is vastly preferable to the alternative.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-2.bg02: Drag my Thufir Hawat card to Secrets to send an Agent there.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-2.bg03: Along with 1 Influence with the Bene Gesserit, this board space has earned you an Intrigue card. It also allows you to steal Intrigue cards, if an opponent is holding four or more.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-2.combat01.pc: This is a new type of Intrigue card: a Combat card. Hold your cursor over it to take a closer look.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-2.combat01.mobile: This is a new type of Intrigue card: a Combat card. Tap and hold it to take a closer look.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-2.combat02: A Combat Intrigue card may only be played during the Conflict at the end of each round. This one lets you spend <sprite name="Spice_2"> to gain 5 <sprite name="Strength">.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-3.duncan01: Face me, Atreides! The favor of witches and nomads is no measure of power. Battle is the true test!
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-3.duncan02: Where Beast is impatient, I must be tranquil. The Conflict will come. For now, I'll reveal my hand.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-3.duncan03: Paul! I hope you've had enough of stuffy Mentats and grouchy warmasters. It's time for me to take over your lessons.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-3.duncan04: Yes, Swordmaster Duncan Idaho has been assigned to be your final tutor. Spend your to acquire his card now.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3.playintrigue01: Look, I'm sure Gurney taught you the basics, but the reality is that you can rarely be sure of the outcome of a battle before it begins.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3.playintrigue02: There's always a chance for the tide to shift. That's because each Leader can play any Combat Intrigue cards they might have.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3.playintrigue03: As the First Player, you get the initial opportunity to play a Combat card. Since you're winning, Pass and let's see what Beast does.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3.playintrigue04: Ha! You've walked straight into my Ambush, fool Atreides!
en_US.tutorial2.turn3.playintrigue05: Well, Paul? Beast has the upper hand. What are you going to do?
en_US.tutorial2.turn3.playintrigue05a: Too easy, Duncan. If I play my Private Army Combat card, I'll regain the lead against Beast.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3.playintrigue06: Impossible! I promise you pain for this insult.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3.playintrigue07: I see I'll need to push you harder! Your reward for winning the Conflict is and 1 Influence with any Faction. Take it with the Fremen.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3.playintrigue08: Your second Influence with a Faction will always earn you a <sprite name="VictoryPoint"> Victory Point. Now hurry up; next round, I'm turning you loose!
en_US.tutorial2.turn4-1.newspaces02: Before you're truly ready to lead, there are a few other board spaces you need to know about.
en_US.tutorial2.turn4-1.newspaces03: The Landsraad Council is where the Great Houses debate and dispense Imperial power. The Hall of Oratory can give you extra Persuasion in a pinch, or you could spend some Solari to Rally Troops.
en_US.tutorial2.turn4-1.newspaces04: Also, you now have access to the Fremen holdfast, Sietch Tabr.
en_US.tutorial2.turn4-1.newspaces05: Leaders must have 2 or more Influence with the Fremen to be permitted to send an Agent there.
en_US.tutorial2.turn4-1.newspaces06.pc: You have many options now; remember that you can hold your cursor over any space to learn more about it.
en_US.tutorial2.turn4-1.newspaces06.mobile: You have many options now; remember that you can tap and hold any space to learn more about it.
en_US.tutorial2.turn4-1.newspaces07: You've seen two significant sources of Victory Points: Conflicts and Influence tracks. Instead of telling you what to do, I'm just going to give you a goal: Reach 4 , however you can.
en_US.tutorial2.trigger.firstreveal01: Paul, before you acquire any cards, notice that a couple are set apart. Arrakis Liaison and The Spice Must Flow are a special type of Imperium card called Reserve cards.
en_US.tutorial2.trigger.firstreveal02: There are many copies of each Reserve card. They remain available after being acquired, instead of being replaced with a new card from the Imperium deck.
en_US.tutorial2.trigger.firstreveal03: The Spice Must Flow is also special in another way: it has an acquire effect, a reward you get as soon as you gain the card. In this case, that's a Victory Point!
en_US.tutorial2.trigger.conflictrewards01: I bet Gurney failed to mention this: The 3rd place Conflict reward is only given out if there are four Leaders in the game!
en_US.tutorial2.trigger.conflictrewards02: While I'm at it, if there's ever a tie for 1st in a Conflict, the tied Leaders all get the 2nd place reward. Likewise, a tie for 2nd results in 3rd place rewards for those Leaders.
en_US.tutorial2.trigger.done01: That wasn't half bad! Your skills are developing quickly, yet I have more to teach you: advanced tactics you'll need when the fight for Arrakis begins in earnest. But let that be a lesson for another day, eh?
en_US.tutorial3.intro01: Welcome back, Paul! I take it you think you're ready to continue your training in advanced tactics?
en_US.tutorial3.intro01b: I've been ready for a long time.
en_US.tutorial3.intro02: You think so? Alright, I'm giving you five goals - but I'll only tell you the first for now.
en_US.tutorial3.intro03: Gain your Swordmaster. The Swordmaster board space costs a hefty Solari. Leaders can only send an Agent there once each game.
en_US.tutorial3.intro04: But, once you do, you'll have an additional permanent Agent to send each round - a considerable advantage.
en_US.tutorial3.intro05: The game has been reset. You'll have a fresh start against Countess Ariana of House Thorvald.
en_US.tutorial3.intro06: From its seat on glorious Ipyr, the Great House Thorvald declares its claim to the fiefdom of Arrakis!
en_US.tutorial3.intro07: Well, they can't all be as charming as Beast, can they? Get to work, Paul! I'll return with more goals as you progress!
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.prescience: Mother says I have the gift of Prescience - I can always see the card on top of my deck. I imagine other Leaders have their own unique abilities.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.mentat-r3: Paul, have you noticed the Mentat board space? It gives you an additional Agent just for this round. Used wisely, it lets you react to your opponents' maneuvers.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.mentat-onuse: I was wondering if you'd notice the Mentat board space! It gives you an additional Agent just for this round. Used wisely, it lets you react to your opponents' maneuvers.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.council: Excellent, Paul, you have your Swordmaster! You can now send it as an additional Agent every round. Next goal: the High Council.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.councilb: Like the Swordmaster space, you can only send an Agent here once per game. Once you have, your seat on the High Council will provide you with an extra every Reveal turn.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.council.early: Quite a move, Paul! By taking a seat on the High Council, you've completed your next goal before I even spoke it! You'll now get an extra Persuasion each Reveal turn.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.alliance01: Prepare yourself: I have a new goal for you! You must gain a Faction Alliance. Each Alliance is worth a to the Leader who secures it.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.alliance02: To gain an Alliance, be the first to reach 4 Influence with a Faction.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.alliance03: Unlike other <sprite name="VictoryPoint">, these can be stolen by your rivals. If they pass you on the Faction's Influence track, they take the Alliance, including the <sprite name="VictoryPoint">! Of course, you can steal from them the same way...
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.alliance01.early: Your opponent just earned a Faction Alliance by being the first Leader to reach 4 Influence with a Faction! Your new goal is to earn one as well. Each Alliance is worth a to the Leader who secures it.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.control01: Paul, I have another goal for you. Look at the Siege of Arrakeen Conflict card. The reward for winning this Conflict includes control of the Arrakeen board space.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.control03: Earning this reward places your Control marker on Arrakeen. While it's there, you earn each time any Leader sends an Agent to that space - including you.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.control04: Also, if a Conflict is revealed for a board space you currently control, you immediately recruit one troop from your supply directly into the Conflict.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.control05: Your goal is to gain control of a board space. If you can, win this Conflict. If not, there will be other opportunities.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.control06: Nice work taking control of that board space!
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.vp: Your abilities continue to improve. One goal left, and it's simple: Reach 5 !
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.vpb: Remember, Influence tracks, Conflicts, and The Spice Must Flow can all be sources of .
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.done01: Son, I've been observing your progress. Soon we will arrive on Arrakis, and these war games will become reality.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.done02: You've performed well. I know that our House will rise high under your leadership.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.trash01: About trashing cards: When you trash, you may choose a card in your hand, your discard pile, or in play to permanently remove from the game.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.trash03: Trashing weaker cards, like many of those in your starting deck, lets you draw your stronger cards more frequently.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.foldspace: About Foldspace: The Spacing Guild Foldspace board space allows you to acquire a special card. It has every Agent icon, and lets you draw a card when played, but then you must trash it, removing it from your deck permanently.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.fremenbond01: The card you're looking at has a Fremen Bond effect. It's only activated if you have at least one other Fremen card in play when you reveal it.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.fremenbond02: You can see a card's Factions here, if it has any.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.endgamecards: About Endgame Intrigue cards: The Intrigue card you just drew has an effect at the end of the game. There will often be conditions for gaining the reward.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.retreat: About retreating troops: You have the option to retreat some of your troops in the Conflict back to your garrison. Retreating can allow you to save troops that may have been overextended.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.endgame: About Endgame: The struggle for Arrakis ends when a Leader has 10 or more at the end of a round, or after the 10th Conflict, whichever comes first. Note that, due to Intrigue cards, the Leader who triggers the endgame may not necessarily be the victor.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.endgameb: In the case of a tie in <sprite name="VictoryPoint">, the Leader with the most resources wins, beginning with spice.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.controlbonus: About Control: Remember: Whenever a Conflict card is revealed for control of a board space that a Leader already controls, they recruit and deploy one troop to the Conflict as a defensive bonus.
en_US.tutorial.trigger.factionbonus: Reaching 4 Influence with a Faction will always earn you that Faction's bonus, whether or not you get their Alliance.
en_US.tutorial03.goal.2-HighCouncil: Take a seat on the High Council.
en_US.tutorial03.goal.4-SpaceControl: Gain control of a board space.
en_US.prompt.first.live.game: Welcome to your first live game. If you do not complete your turns in the time allotted, your turn will be taken by an AI. If an AI takes your turn two times in a row you will be resigned. Have fun and make sure not to go anywhere!
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent04.gamepad: To send an Agent to a board space, first choose a card to play. Press to view your Reconnaissance card.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent07.gamepad: Press to select Reconnaissance as the card you are going to send to the city of Arrakeen.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent08.gamepad: Now I press again on Arrakeen to send my Agent!
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-1.Agent12.gamepad: Your first Agent turn is over. To send another Agent, you'll need to wait until your next turn. Hold <sprite name="xbutton"> to end your turn.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal03.gamepad: Unlike an Agent turn, at the start of a Reveal turn you play all the remaining cards in your hand. Hold to take your Reveal turn.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.conflict02.gamepad: The Conflict card shows what's at stake. Press on it for a closer look.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.intrigue01.gamepad: Carthag gave you a new kind of card: an Intrigue card. Press on it for a closer look.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.deploy03b.gamepad: Deploying doesn't happen automatically. When you're ready, press on Deploy Units.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-1.deploy05.gamepad: You just recruited a troop from Carthag, so this turn you can deploy up to three troops. Use three times to increase your troops then hold to confirm.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-2.gurney02.gamepad: Yes, but I've got something he won't see coming. Press on my card.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.moretroops04.gamepad: It's time to spring the trap. Press on my card's Reveal effect to use it.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-2.combat01.gamepad: This is a new type of Intrigue card: a Combat card. Press on it to take a closer look.
en_US.tutorial2.turn4-1.newspaces06.gamepad: You have many options now; remember that you can press <sprite name="ybutton"> on a space to learn more about it.
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-3.reveal06b.gamepad: Press on our Warmaster, Gurney Halleck's card to acquire it for .
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.thufir04.gamepad: Don't you? You've forgotten your <sprite name="IntrigueCard"> Intrigue card. Press <sprite name="abutton"> to play it now.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-2.bg02.gamepad: Play my Thufir Hawat card to Secrets to send an Agent there.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3-1.fremen02.gamepad: To send an Agent to a Faction space, you must play a card with that Faction's Agent icon. Diplomacy has all four Faction icons - Play it to Stillsuits.

en_US.hagal.desc:
Play against two rivals from the House Hagal!

Rivals use streamlined rules, but they will still give you a challenge by competing for board spaces and Influence, fighting in conflicts, and collecting Victory Points.

On a Rival's turn, they will draw a card from the House Hagal deck and place an Agent on the space it shows, gaining related benefits.

If they collect enough of any given resource, a Rival will gain a Victory Point. They also score VPs from Alliance tokens, and winning Conflicts.

Do not underestimate House Hagal! It will take all of your cunning to wrest Arrakis from their hands.
en_US.scenario.AncientDuel.name: Ancient Duel
en_US.scenario.AncientDuel.flavor: May thy knife chip and shatter.
en_US.scenario.AncientDuel.normal.description: At the start of each Combat, each player with at least one deployed troop draws an Intrigue card.
en_US.scenario.AncientDuel.heroic.description: At the start of each round, each opponent recruits a troop. At the start of each Combat, each player with at least one deployed troop draws an Intrigue card.
en_US.scenario.BeneGesseritInitiation.name: Bene Gesserit Initiation
en_US.scenario.BeneGesseritInitiation.flavor: Do you often dream things that happen just as you dreamed them?
en_US.scenario.BeneGesseritInitiation.normal.d: You start with a Missionaria Protectiva in your deck instead of a Reconnaissance. Whenever you acquire a Bene Gesserit card, . Opponents start with 1 Influence with another Faction.
en_US.scenario.BeneGesseritInitiation.heroic.d: You start with a Missionaria Protectiva in your deck instead of a Reconnaissance. Whenever you acquire a Bene Gesserit card, . Opponents start with 1 Influence with each other Faction. You can’t win until you have trashed your entire starting deck other than Signet Ring and Missionaria Protectiva.
en_US.scenario.DesertPower.name: Desert Power
en_US.scenario.DesertPower.flavor: Rolling over the sands, you can see spice in the air.
en_US.scenario.DesertPower.normal.description: You start with a Spice Hunter instead of a Diplomacy. Whenever you acquire a Fremen card, recruit and deploy one troop to the Conflict. Opponents start with control of an Arrakis board space.
en_US.scenario.DesertPower.heroic.description: You start with a Crysknife instead of a Diplomacy. Whenever you acquire a Fremen card, gain . Opponents start with control of an Arrakis board space. You can’t win unless you control at least two board spaces.
en_US.scenario.EyeoftheStorm.name: Eye of the Storm
en_US.scenario.EyeoftheStorm.flavor: You fight when the necessity arises, no matter the mood.
en_US.scenario.EyeoftheStorm.normal.descriptio: Randomize the order of the Conflict Deck.
en_US.scenario.EyeoftheStorm.heroic.descriptio: Conflict IIs in the Conflict Deck are replaced with extra copies of Conflict IIIs. You start with a Scout on top of your deck, and your opponents start with three extra troops in their garrisons.
en_US.scenario.FencingMirror.name: Fencing Mirror
en_US.scenario.FencingMirror.flavor: Dreams make good stories, but everything important happens when we’re awake.
en_US.scenario.FencingMirror.normal.descriptio: Whenever a player acquires a card from the Imperium Row, they acquire an additional copy of it.
en_US.scenario.FencingMirror.heroic.descriptio: Whenever a player acquires a card from the Imperium Row or Reserve, they acquire an additional copy of it. Opponents start with a Gurney Halleck in their deck.
en_US.scenario.GreatAlliance.name: Great Alliance
en_US.scenario.GreatAlliance.flavor: Every morning, I ask myself: What is the meaning of this day? And then I remember: to make the best possible alliance.
en_US.scenario.GreatAlliance.normal.descriptio: Faction Alliances are worth an additional <sprite name="VictoryPoint">.
en_US.scenario.GreatAlliance.heroic.descriptio: Faction Alliances are worth an additional <sprite name="VictoryPoint"> to your opponents. You can’t win unless you have at least two Alliances.
en_US.scenario.ImperialBeneficence.name: Imperial Beneficence
en_US.scenario.ImperialBeneficence.flavor: When is a gift not a gift?
en_US.scenario.ImperialBeneficence.normal.desc: You begin the game with a Sardaukar Infantry and no Convincing Arguments. At the end of each turn in which you played or revealed an Emperor card, gain for every 2 Emperor Influence you have. You can’t win unless you have the most .
en_US.scenario.ImperialBeneficence.heroic.desc: At the end of each turn in which you played or revealed an Emperor card, gain <sprite name="Solari_1"> for every 2 Emperor Influence you have. You can’t win unless you have the Emperor Alliance and at least twice as much <sprite name="Solari"> as any opponent. You may not send Agents to Fremen board spaces or acquire Fremen cards.
en_US.scenario.JourneyThroughArrakis.name: Across the Imperium
en_US.scenario.JourneyThroughArrakis.flavor: Without change something sleeps inside us, and seldom awakens. The sleeper must awaken
en_US.scenario.JourneyThroughArrakis.normal.de: You can’t win unless you've sent an Agent to each non-<sprite name="Landsraad"> board space.
en_US.scenario.JourneyThroughArrakis.heroic.de: You can’t win unless you've sent an Agent to each board space.
en_US.scenario.MercenaryAgents.name: Mercenary Agents
en_US.scenario.MercenaryAgents.flavor: They see what they’ve been told to see.
en_US.scenario.MercenaryAgents.normal.descript: You have unlimited Agents, but must pay for each Agent you send beyond the first each round. You also start with the Intrigue card Windfall.
en_US.scenario.MercenaryAgents.heroic.descript: You have unlimited Agents, but must pay for each Agent you send beyond the first each round. Opponents start with a seat on the High Council.
en_US.scenario.MindKiller.name: Mind Killer
en_US.scenario.MindKiller.flavor: An animal caught in a trap will gnaw off Its own leg to escape. What will you do?
en_US.scenario.MindKiller.normal.description: At the start of each Combat, every player with no deployed troops trashes the top card of their deck.
en_US.scenario.MindKiller.heroic.description: At the start of each Combat, every player with no deployed troops trashes the top card of their deck. You don't receive rewards for anything except first place in a Conflict.
en_US.scenario.ShiftingSands.name: Shifting Sands
en_US.scenario.ShiftingSands.flavor: I said I would not harm them, and I shall not. But Arrakis is Arrakis, and the desert takes the weak.
en_US.scenario.ShiftingSands.normal.descriptio: At the start of each round, the Imperium Row is removed and replaced.
en_US.scenario.ShiftingSands.heroic.descriptio: At the start of each round, the Imperium Row is removed and replaced. Then, each opponent acquires a different one of the lowest cost cards that were removed.
en_US.scenario.TheKwisatzHaderach.name: The Kwisatz Haderach
en_US.scenario.TheKwisatzHaderach.flavor: One day, a legend will be born. All of civilization depends on it.
en_US.scenario.TheKwisatzHaderach.normal.descr: You start with Kwisatz Haderach, in hand but only one Agent.
en_US.scenario.TheKwisatzHaderach.heroic.descr:
You start with only one Agent and Urgent Mission. You also start with Kwisatz Haderach and Lady Jessica on top of your deck.
Opponents start with their Swordmaster.
en_US.scenario.TheLongGame.name: The Long Game
en_US.scenario.TheLongGame.flavor: A great man doesn't seek to lead. He's called to it.
en_US.scenario.TheLongGame.normal.description: The threshold for triggering the end game is raised to 12 <sprite name="VictoryPoint">. Each player starts with a smaller deck. An additional copy of each Conflict III is added to the Conflict Deck.
en_US.scenario.TheLongGame.heroic.description: The threshold for triggering the end game is raised to 13 <sprite name="VictoryPoint">. Each player starts with a smaller deck and your opponents start with 3 <sprite name="VictoryPoint">. An additional copy of each Conflict III is added to the Conflict Deck.
en_US.scenario.TheSpiceMustPour.name: The Spice Must Pour
en_US.scenario.TheSpiceMustPour.flavor: My road leads into the desert.
en_US.scenario.TheSpiceMustPour.normal.descrip: You start the game with a Spice Smuggler instead of a Seek Allies. The Spice Must Flow costs you 1 less for each Spacing Guild card you've played this round. You can’t win unless you've acquired at least 2 The Spice Must Flow.
en_US.scenario.TheSpiceMustPour.heroic.descrip: You start the game with a Space Travel instead of a Diplomacy. The Spice Must Flow costs you 1 less for each Spacing Guild card you've played this round. You can’t win unless you've acquired at least 4 The Spice Must Flow.
en_US.challenges.description: Put your training to the test in this series of games with unique rules, goals, and starting conditions. Each challenge has a more difficult "heroic" version to unlock by getting 1st place in its normal version.

en_US.gameoptions.epicmode.description:
For players wishing to play a longer game.
- Game end triggers at 12 VP
- Conflict deck contains 5 Conflict IIs followed by 5 Conflict IIIs
- 1 copy of Dune, the Desert Planet in each starting deck is replaced with 1 copy of Control the Spice.
- Each player starts with 1 Intrigue card.
- Each player begins with 5 troops in their garrison (instead of 3)
en_US.gameoptions.epicmode.immo.description:
For players wishing to play a longer game.
- Game end triggers at 12 VP.
- Each player starts with 1 Intrigue card.
- Each player begins with 5 troops in their garrison.
- One Control the Spice begins the game in each player's discard pile.
- The Conflict deck is made up of 5 Conflict II's followed by 5 Conflict III's.
en_US.playonline.live.halftime.description:
Live
Best for those who want to play a game in a single session. Players have 90 seconds to complete a turn in a Live game. If a player exceeds that time, their turn is taken by an AI. If an AI takes a turn for a player two times in a row or a player does not take the first move of the game for themselves, that player is permanently replaced by the AI.

en_US.store.product.riseofix.name: Rise of Ix
en_US.store.product.riseofix.description:
Acquire technology for lasting benefits. Dominate the battlefield with mighty dreadnoughts. Outmaneuver your opponents by dispatching infiltrators. Experience the new Epic Mode for a longer, high-stakes challenge. Let your fortunes ascend with Rise of Ix.

The struggle for control of the Imperium continues! Technological innovations from the planet Ix offer strategic advantages to those able to acquire them. The spreading reach of the CHOAM corporation provides trade resources to fuel your climb to power. Familiar strategies take on new dimensions as fearsome warships reshape the conflict on Arrakis. And the Leaders of three more Great Houses enter the fray.
en_US.store.product.immortality.name: Immortality
en_US.store.product.immortality.description:
As the Great Houses wage war, the Bene Tleilax advance their own agenda by trading in genetic innovations. Will you hire Face Dancer spies of unmatched skill? Regrow damaged tissue and organs? Or dare to employ people restored to life as gholas.

Immortality expands Dune: Imperium in new directions. Make shadowy deals with the Tleilaxu to harvest genetic specimens. Unlock the potential of scientific research. Graft cards together to empower your Agents.
en_US.store.product.uprising.name: Uprising
en_US.store.product.uprising.description:
After betraying and destroying House Atreides, the Emperor Shaddam Corrino IV has given House Harkonnen control over the planet Arrakis once more. But a mysterious warrior named Muad’Dib has risen to power among the Fremen, threatening the schemes of the Emperor and his allies.

This major expansion for Dune: Imperium Digital transforms the core experience with a new Imperium deck, reimagined conflicts, fresh leaders, and updated spaces to send your agents.

In Uprising, you want to continue to balance military might with political intrigue, wielding new tools in pursuit of victory. Spies will shore up your plans. Vital contracts will expand your resources. Or learn the ways of the Fremen and ride mighty sandworms into battle!
Continue saved game or start a new attempt? Starting a new attempt will forfeit your last attempt where scores contribute to the leaderboard until the next Skirmish.

en_US.prompt.reputation.ftt.body:
To encourage fair play and game completion, every player now has a Rep score ranging from 0 to 50. This score is shared between ranked play and lobby games.

 * Starting Point: All players begin with 30 Rep.
 * Earning Rep: Gain 1 Rep for every game you complete.
 * Losing Rep: Resigning or timing out of a live or ranked game deducts 4 Rep (unless all opponents had been replaced by AI). Resigning or timing out of an asych game deducts 2 Rep.

Key Rules:
 * You can set a minimum Rep requirement for joining lobby games you create. Players without enough Rep will not see your game in the lobby.
 * A minimum of 1 Rep is required to participate in ranked play. If your Rep falls below 1, you’ll need to complete lobby games to rebuild your score.

Stay in the game, build your Rep, and have fun!

Combat Space Gain Maker Hooks, 1 water, and recruit 1 troops OR gain 1 water and you may destroy the Shield Wall. (The Shield Wall prevents sandworms from being summoned during certain Conflicts.)

en_US.tooltip.space.deepdesert: Deep Desert Spice Trade Cost: Combat Space Gain any bonus spice accumulated here. Choose: Gain 4 spice or, if you have Maker Hooks, you may summon 2 sandworms.
en_US.tooltip.gameoption.brutalescalation: Brutal Escalation\nRivals flip two cards during Conflict IIIs and add the swords from both to their strength.
en_US.tooptip.gameoption.smartpolitics: Smart Politics\nRivals pursue Faction Influence more efficiently.
en_US.tooltip.shieldwall.intact: Shield Wall\nThe Shield Wall prevents sandworms from being summoned to Conflicts with the Shield Wall icon.
en_US.tooltip.shieldwall.destroyed: Shield Wall\nThe Shield Wall has been destroyed and no longer prevents sandworm from being summoned!
en_US.tooltip.hooks: Maker Hooks\nMaker Hooks allow you to summon worms to battle from Hagga Basin and Deep Desert.
en_US.tooltip.choammodule: The CHOAM Module adds contracts - short-term goals you can collect and complete for rewards.
en_US.tooltip.spies:
Spy Supply
Spies can be placed on observation posts, then recalled when sending an agent to a connected space to gather intelligence (draw a card) or infiltrate a space occupied by an enemy agent.
en_US.tooltip.recall: Recall an Agent you didn't send this turn to your supply.
en_US.tooltip.ladyjessica.memories: Memories\nWhen Lady Jessica sends an Agent to a board space, she may return all these memories to her supply, drawing a card for each one. Then, she becomes Reverend Mother Jessica.
en_US.hanger.description.battleicon: Earn battle icons by winning Conflicts. When you collect 2 of the same icon, they turn into a Victory Point.
en_US.hanger.description.spy: Place a Spy on an available observation post.\nSpies can be used to Infiltrate spaces and Gather Intelligence (draw cards) when sending an Agent to a connected board space.
en_US.hanger.description.recallspy: Recall one of your Spies to your supply.
en_US.hanger.description.worm: Worms are 3 <sprite name="Strength"> units which can't be retreated. When you win a Conflict with a worm, you double the rewards (not including battle icons).
en_US.hanger.description.makerhooks: Maker Hooks allow you to summon worms to battle from Hagga Basin and Deep Desert.
en_US.hanger.description.recallagent: Return an Agent that you did not send this turn to your supply.
en_US.hanger.description.contract: Take one of the available contracts. Complete it later to gain its reward.
en_US.hanger.description.blowwall: You may destroy the Shield Wall, allowing sandworms to be summoned to any Conflict.
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.thufir05b: You can also double-click to acquire a card (or play one).
en_US.tutorial1.turn2-3.thufir05b.mobile: You can also double-tap to acquire a card (or play one).
en_US.tutorial1.turn1-2.spice02.gamepad: My Dune, the Desert Planet cards have a icon - I'll play one to Hagga Basin to send my second Agent there.
en_US.tutorial2.turn3.playintrigue03.gamepad: As the First Player, you get the initial opportunity to play a Combat card. Since you're winning, hold to Pass and let's see what Beast does.
en_US.tutorial3.trigger.prescience.gamepad: Mother says I have the gift of Prescience - I can always see the card on top of my deck by pressing on its preview image. I imagine other Leaders have their own unique abilities.
en_US.tutorialroi.intro01: Welcome back, Paul, and congratulations on your successes. You've taken to leadership admirably.
en_US.tutorialroi.intro02: I fight when the necessity arises.
en_US.tutorialroi.intro03: Just so. However, in Rise of Ix there are several new board spaces and a few new concepts to master if you want to stay on top in the struggle for supremacy over Arrakis.
en_US.tutorialroi.ship01: The Shipping track, for example, is a vital tool for managing your resources.
en_US.tutorialroi.ship02: You begin the game with a Freighter on the origin space of the track.
en_US.tutorialroi.ship03: <sprite name="Freighter"> is the Freighter icon. You can see it on both of the new CHOAM board spaces.
en_US.tutorialroi.ship06: Whenever you gain a , you have a choice: you may advance your Freighter, moving it one space up the Shipping track...
en_US.tutorialroi.ship07: ...or you may recall it to the Freighter's origin.
en_US.tutorialroi.ship08: When you recall, you immediately gain the benefits of the space your Freighter was recalled from - as well as the benefits of each space beneath that one on the track.
en_US.tutorialroi.ship09: Since you're currently at the origin, you must advance. Then, end your turn.
en_US.tutorialroi.ship10: Good. Note that sending an Agent to Interstellar Shipping, which gives , requires you to have 2 Influence with the Spacing Guild.
en_US.tutorialroi.ship11: Now a test: advance your Freighter to the top position on the Shipping track and recall it from there.
en_US.tutorialroi.ship12: I'm giving you 1 Influence with the <sprite name="SpacingGuild"> Spacing Guild to help get you started. Show me what you can do.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech01: You've learned well and can now reap the benefits.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech02: You may choose to gain your rewards from the Shipping track in any order you wish. You'll recruit 2 troops and gain an Influence with a Faction of your choice.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech05: You also gain either <sprite name="Spice_2"> or <sprite name="Solari_5">. If you choose <sprite name="Solari_5">, each other player will also get <sprite name="Solari_1">.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech06: For now, choose the <sprite name="Spice_2"> option.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech07: Finally, the top space of the Shipping track has a new icon. It indicates that you can purchase a Tech from the Tech Offer on Ix.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech08: Ix is well known across the Imperium for its advanced technology.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech09: At the start of the game, three Techs are made available in the Tech Offer.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech10: Whenever you gain an Acquire Tech icon, you may choose one Tech from the Tech Offer and pay its cost in spice to acquire it.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech11: The <sprite name="BuyTech_MinusTwo"> effect on the Shipping track has an additional benefit - it gives a <sprite name="Spice_2"> discount to the Tech you acquire.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech13: It's added to your Tech area here as a new Tech replaces it in the Tech Offer.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech14: Techs can provide different kinds of benefits. Some will be persistent, while others happen at specific times.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech15: Certain Techs, like your Training Drones, can be flipped once per round to gain their effect.
en_US.tutorialroi.tech16: Use Training Drones to recruit a troop.
en_US.tutorialroi.techneg01: Good. Now, the Shipping track isn't the only way you can acquire Techs, which brings us to another new board space.
en_US.tutorialroi.techneg02: This is Tech Negotiation, a Landsraad board space. It has multiple effects.
en_US.tutorialroi.techneg03: First, it grants you an extra <sprite name="Persuasion_1"> during your Reveal turn.
en_US.tutorialroi.techneg04: Additionally, it offers a choice: you can either acquire a Tech at a discount, or you can gain a Tech Negotiator.
en_US.tutorialroi.techneg05: When you gain a <sprite name="TechNegotiator">, a troop from your supply turns into a Tech Negotiator. Whenever you acquire a Tech, the cost is reduced by <sprite name="Spice_1"> for each Tech Negotiator you return to your supply.
en_US.tutorialroi.dread01: Now that you understand Tech, there's one last new board space for you to learn about.
en_US.tutorialroi.dread02: The dreadnought space also allows you to acquire a Tech; however, its primary function is to commission a dreadnought to your garrison.
en_US.tutorialroi.dread03: A dreadnought is a new type of Combat unit with several powerful features. Your next goal is to obtain one. Keep in mind it will cost <sprite name="Solari_3"> to commission.
en_US.tutorialroi.control01: I've done it. How can I make use of this dreadnought?
en_US.tutorialroi.control02: Dreadnoughts can be deployed to a Conflict just like troops can, in the place of a troop. They add <sprite name="Strength"><sprite name="Strength"><sprite name="Strength"> to your Combat total.
en_US.tutorialroi.control03: They cannot be destroyed - at the end of any Conflict you don't win, they return to your garrison and may be redeployed in the future. Bear in mind that you can never have more than two.
en_US.tutorialroi.control04: Your final goal: win a Conflict using your dreadnought. You will be opposed by Archduke Armand Ecaz.
en_US.tutorialroi.control05: The Atreides have had their chance. It's time for House Ecaz to rule Arrakis.
en_US.tutorialroi.control06: The enemy was no match for the power of my dreadnought.
en_US.tutorialroi.control07: A great victory, Lisan al Gaib.
en_US.tutorialroi.control08: When you win a Conflict using a dreadnought, you get to send it to take control of one of these board spaces on Arrakis.
en_US.tutorialroi.control09: A dreadnought placed this way covers any existing control marker, temporarily taking control from the space's prior owner.
en_US.tutorialroi.control10: Choose a board space to take control of it.
en_US.tutorialroi.control11: After the next round's Conflict, the dreadnought returns to its owner's garrison and control of the space is relinquished.
en_US.tutorialroi.end1: I think you're ready to take the fight to the Harkonnen.
en_US.tutorialroi.end2: I'll make them regret their crimes against my House...
en_US.tutorialroi.trigger.discard: <sprite name="Discard"> Discard is a new icon which means "discard a card from your hand." You cannot discard Intrigue cards to it.
en_US.tutorialroi.trigger.unload01: <sprite name="Unload"> Unload is a new ability attached to the reveal boxes of certain cards. It means that whenever that card is discarded or trashed, you immediately gain the unload effect shown.
en_US.tutorialroi.trigger.unload02: You can also get these effects normally by revealing the card during your Reveal turn.
en_US.tutorialroi.trigger.infiltrate: Some Agent icons look like this. They can be used to send Agents to matching board spaces even if an opponent's Agent is already there - this infiltration effect bypasses them entirely.
en_US.tutorialroi.trigger.recall: Did you forget? Your goal is to recall your Freighter from the top space of the Shipping track. Undo that action and try again.
en_US.tutorialroi.goal.1-Shipping: Recall your Freighter from the top of the Shipping track.
en_US.tutorialroi.goal.3-Control: Win a Conflict using a dreadnought.
en_US.tutorial.description.tutorial04: Learn the basics of Rise of Ix: Shipping, Tech, and dreadnoughts.
en_US.tutorialimm.intro01: The shadows around our House grow longer. Are you prepared to do what is necessary?
en_US.tutorialimm.research01: The first thing you need to know about Dune Imperium: Immortality is that your starting deck has changed. In place of the 2 copies of Dune, the Desert Planet, you now have access to Experimentation.
en_US.tutorialimm.research02: Experimentation is one of the places you can find the new research icon.
en_US.tutorialimm.research03: Research... does this have something to do with the rumors I've heard about recent scientific advances?
en_US.tutorialimm.research04: It does. The Bene Tleilax are a powerful fringe society in the Imperium, specializing in genetic engineering. Use Experimentation to send an Agent to Hagga Basin.
en_US.tutorialimm.research04.gamepad: It does. The Bene Tleilax are a powerful fringe society in the Imperium, specializing in genetic engineering. Use Experimentation to send an Agent to Hagga Basin.
en_US.tutorialimm.research06: This is the research track. It charts the progress of the scientific work the Bene Tleilax perform on behalf of our House.
en_US.tutorialimm.research07: Your token starts on the left side. When you gain a <sprite name="Research"> research, as you just did, you advance one space right.
en_US.tutorialimm.research08: When you reach a space on the research track, you immediately gain any benefits on that space.
en_US.tutorialimm.research10: This is a genetic specimen. The Bene Tleilax both use and produce them in the course of their work.
en_US.tutorialimm.research11b: You've made a good start. Use your other Experimentation to send an Agent to Secure Contract.
en_US.tutorialimm.research11b.gamepad: You've made a good start but you should keep it going. Use your other Experimentation to send an Agent to Secure Contract.
en_US.tutorialimm.research12: Once again, you gain a <sprite name="Research">, which will advance your research token.
en_US.tutorialimm.research13: When there's a choice, you decide which direction to move. Try moving down and right.
en_US.tutorialimm.research15: The Tleilaxu icon represents embracing those works of the Bene Tleilax's which are the least savory. Each time you gain one, you advance along this track.
en_US.tutorialimm.research16: There are significant benefits to be gained in this manner, if your conscience can bear it.
en_US.tutorialimm.tleilaxu02: You're used to acquiring cards from the Imperium Row. Immortality introduces the Tleilaxu Row as a new source of cards.
en_US.tutorialimm.tleilaxu03: Here, the Bene Tleilax make their... innovations available. However, Persuasion isn't what they're after.
en_US.tutorialimm.tleilaxu04: Let me guess... I'll need to spend <sprite name="Specimen"> specimens during my Reveal turn to get them.
en_US.tutorialimm.tleilaxu06: There are two normal slots in the Tleilaxu Row. When you acquire a card from one of these, it goes to your discard pile as usual and is replaced by another random Tleilaxu card.
en_US.tutorialimm.tleilaxu07: The final slot in the Tleilaxu Row is for the reserve card Reclaimed Forces. When you pay for this card, you gain its acquire effect but it's not added to your deck.
en_US.tutorialimm.tleilaxu08: The one specimen you've gained is enough to acquire Contaminator from the Bene Tleilax.
en_US.tutorialimm.tleilaxu08.gamepad: The one specimen you've gained is enough to acquire Contaminator from the Bene Tleilax.
en_US.tutorialimm.tleilaxu09: You can also, as usual, spend your Persuasion to acquire cards from the Imperium Row. Take Planned Coupling.
en_US.tutorialimm.tleilaxu10.gamepad: You can also, as usual, spend your Persuasion to acquire cards from the Imperium Row. Take Planned Coupling.
en_US.tutorialimm.tleilaxu11: We'll skip the Conflict for now. End your turn.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft01: Use your Signet Ring to send an Agent to Arrakeen.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft01.gamepad: Use your Signet Ring to send an Agent to Arrakeen.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft03: Planned Coupling has an important new ability for you to master.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft03.gamepad: Planned Coupling has an important new ability for you to master.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft04: Some cards in Immortality can be combined with other cards when used to send an Agent. The Bene Tleilax call this technique Graft.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft05: Graft cards can never be used alone to send an Agent. You must always play them with exactly one other card during an Agent turn.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft06: When you do, you can use an Agent icon from either card to send the Agent.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft08: This effect on the board space and the card in your play area indicates your opportunity to graft. Now play Experimentation.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft08.gamepad: This effect on the board space and the card in your play area indicates your opportunity to graft. Now play Experimentation.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft09: Is it good to graft cards?
en_US.tutorialimm.graft10: It can be. One major benefit is that grafting lets you use the Agent box effects of both cards.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft11: Draw a card and advance your research token.
en_US.tutorialimm.graft12: Which direction would you like to advance your research?
en_US.tutorialimm.markers01: I've drawn an Intrigue card with symbols I remember seeing on the research track.
en_US.tutorialimm.markers01.gamepad: I've drawn an Intrigue card with symbols I remember seeing on the research track.
en_US.tutorialimm.markers02: Good eye. Certain cards have genetic marker effects that only work if you've advanced far enough in your research.
en_US.tutorialimm.markers03: Once you reach this part of the track, effects with a single genetic marker become enabled.
en_US.tutorialimm.markers04: To activate effects with a <sprite name="GeneticMarker2"> double genetic marker, you must be at the end of the track.
en_US.tutorialimm.ifgrafted02: Keep an eye out for cards like this one. It doesn't have graft itself, but if you play it with a graft card to send an Agent, you'll gain an extra benefit.
en_US.tutorialimm.ifgrafted03: Acquire any cards you like and end your turn. Unlike Persuasion, specimens you don't spend will carry over to your next turn.
en_US.tutorialimm.atomics01: You're learning fast. One more thing – you have a new tool at your disposal: Family Atomics.
en_US.tutorialimm.atomics02: Each player gets one Atomics token at the start of the game, and may use it during their turn to remove and replace the entire Imperium Row.
en_US.tutorialimm.atomics03: That sounds like it could be useful for finding the cards I need.
en_US.tutorialimm.outro01: It's time to test your progress. Use what you've learned to reach 5 <sprite name="VictoryPoint">.
en_US.tutorialimm.outro02: You will be opposed by Count Ilban Richese.
en_US.tutorialimm.outro03: The help of the abominable Tleilaxu doesn't make you a match for my House.
en_US.tutorialimm.station01: Look out: the Research Station has changed. It now provides two cards and a research.
en_US.tutorialimm.victory: Your father would be proud to see the leader you've become.
en_US.ftt.specimensupply.1: Be aware that your troops and specimens are pulled from the same 12 cube supply.
en_US.ftt.specimensupply.2: If you run out of troops and need to recruit more you can pull from your specimens - but the reverse isn't possible.
en_US.ftt.graft.1: You just drew a card with Graft. Graft cards can't be played to send an Agent on their own.
en_US.ftt.graft.2: To play a card with graft, drag it to the board space you want to send an Agent to. Then, drag the card you want to graft to it out of your hand.
en_US.ftt.graft.2.gamepad: To play a card with graft, select it, and select the board space you want to send an Agent to. Then, select the card you want to graft to it.
en_US.ftt.graft.3: You can also do this in the opposite order.
en_US.tutorialimm.trigger.conditionalicon01: This is a special type of card that only has Agent icons if you meet a certain condition.
en_US.tutorialimm.trigger.conditionalicon02: The condition varies, depending on the card.
en_US.tutorialimm.trigger.tleilaxufirst: Unlike other rewards, only the first player to reach this space on the Tleilaxu track gains .
en_US.tutorialimm.trigger.graftreveal: When you reveal a graft card, it works just like any normal card.
en_US.tutorialimm.trigger.firstgenetic: When you reach this column, for the rest of the game, any Tleilaxu cards you acquire may be placed directly on top of your deck.
en_US.tutorialimm.trigger.secondgenetic: When you reach this column, for the rest of the game, whenever you gain <sprite name="Research"> research, you draw a card instead of advancing.
en_US.tutorialimm.trigger.hagal: When a Hagal card with this icon is revealed, one of the cards in the Tleilaxu Row is discarded.
en_US.tooltip.tutorialuprising: Learn the basics of Uprising: sandworms and the Shield Wall, Spies, battle icons, contracts, and the new board.
en_US.tutorialup.trigger.tsmf: The Spice Must Flow is a little different: now it's a Spacing Guild card. Look out for effects which can use this.
en_US.tutorialup.trigger.contractlimit: There are a limited number of contracts. Once they're all gone, if a player would take a contract, instead they gain <sprite name="Solari_2">.
en_US.tutorialup.trigger.contractsmodule: This game is being played without the contracts module. Whenever a player would take a contract, instead they gain <sprite name="Solari_2">.
en_US.tutorialup.trigger.contracts: Some contracts work a bit differently. They may want you to harvest a certain amount of spice in a turn or acquire a The Spice Must Flow. Some even complete themselves immediately!
en_US.tutorialup.trigger.spy: If you need to place a Spy while you already have 3, you can move one of your existing Spies instead. This counts as recalling a Spy.
en_US.tutorialup.trigger.spyagent: Cards with this Agent icon can be used to send an Agent to any board space you're spying on.
en_US.up.highcouncil.1: Now that you have a seat on the High Council, you have access to this space's alternate mode.
en_US.up.highcouncil.2: For the rest of the game, you can send an Agent here to gain two spice, 3 troops, and draw an Intrigue card.

en_US.worm1101.title: Shipping Magnate

en_US.worm1104.text: Score all four conditions with the Grand Conspiracy Intrigue card.

en_US.worm1202.text: Reach the end of the research track.
en_US.worm1202.title: Twisted Experimentation

en_US.worm1312.title: Council Coup

en_US.prompt.skirmish.scoringmethods.31:
Trash to Treasure

en_US.prompt.skirmish.scoringmethods.32:
Interplanetary Shipment

en_US.prompt.skirmish.scoringmethods.33:
Cargo Run

en_US.prompt.skirmish.scoringmethods.34:
Ixian Supremacy

Area Control

Twisted Experimentation

en_US.prompt.skirmish.scoringmethods.38:
Experimental Trials
